prose.summary: The hardwood bedroom furniture meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed under the India-UAE CEPA. This results in an estimated saving of 7500.00 AED for this shipment. Please refer to the claim checklist below for the next steps.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 94036000, Other wooden furniture. Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal import duty rate (MFN rate), which is charged when no preference is claimed, is 20%, while the reduced CEPA rate is 12.5%. The CEPA rate applies to Basic Customs Duty only, so other import charges such as IGST are still paid. Claiming this preference on a shipment value of 100000 AED gives an estimated saving of 7500.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff heading (CTH), meaning each non-originating input must be classified in a different 4-digit heading than the product, plus value addition (VA) of at least 40%, which is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials. The price basis is FOB, the price of the goods loaded on board at the UAE port. The product meets this rule because the final manufacture took place in the UAE and the work went beyond minimal operations. All 2 non-originating inputs are classified outside heading 9403, satisfying the CTH check, and the value addition is 52.0%, which is above the 40% threshold.

notes.text: Preference is only given to originating goods shipped directly from the UAE to India. If your shipment transits through another country, it must remain under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, or storage.
The agreement is unclear on whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same value-addition threshold, except for a 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The '+' in the rule 'CTH + VA 40%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual duty amounts will differ from the estimate based on the shipment value given.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

Preference is given only to originating goods shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from a secondary source (CBIC Instruction 28/2022), not confirmed from the official text.
